chapters.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
chapters.fact: This is where Perseverance’s surface journey began. NASA named the landing site for science-fiction author Octavia E. Butler.

chapters.name: Seitah wheel tracks
chapters.fact: Perseverance explored sand and exposed rocks at Seitah before returning toward the delta. Wheel tracks mark its passage through this early chapter of the mission.

chapters.name: Wildcat Ridge & Skinner Ridge
chapters.fact: These neighboring rocks preserve different sediments. Skinner Ridge contains larger rock and mineral fragments; Wildcat Ridge is much finer grained. Comparing them helps explain how material moved through the ancient delta.

chapters.name: Belva from Echo Creek
chapters.fact: An impact opened Belva crater through older rocks of Jezero’s delta. The exposed layers let scientists look inside deposits that were already here before the crater formed.

chapters.name: Neretva Vallis
chapters.fact: Neretva Vallis once carried water into Jezero. Billions of years later, its channel offered Perseverance a way around difficult boulder terrain on the approach to Bright Angel.

chapters.name: Jezero rim
chapters.fact: Perseverance reached the top of Jezero’s rim in December 2024, leaving the crater interior behind for a new chapter of exploration.

chapters.name: The western frontier
chapters.fact: You have followed our adaptation of Perseverance’s recorded journey through sol 1980. This is the endpoint of this game’s pinned route snapshot, not the end of the real mission.
